# Module: runtime-cli

## Scope
Owns the terminal entrypoint, deterministic shell orchestrators, worker coordination scripts, command wrappers, and install-time CLI wiring.

**Primary paths:** `install.sh`, `plugins/edc/scripts/`, `plugins/edc/commands/`.

## Purpose
This module turns EDC prompt bundles into reproducible workflows. The public `edc` command parses user intent, review scope, model/runtime options, and context mode, then delegates to shell orchestrators that own build/update/review/delivery/quality control flow. Shell and small Node helpers own routing, freshness recovery, task manifests, bounded worker pools, staging, promotion, validation, structured result files, and backend spawning; models receive one declared task and output set and must not choose process flags or launch nested agents.

The current runtime has three review lenses: `edc review`/`review-all` resolves one immutable candidate, prepares context once, and runs security, delivery/architecture, then quality phases serially by default; exact `EDC_PARALLEL=1` opts back into concurrent lens execution, and surviving phases are not cancelled when a sibling fails. `security-review` is security/adversarial only; `delivery-review` checks goal/spec delivery plus architecture fit; `quality-review` runs the code-quality/maintainability audit pipeline, with `audit` kept as a deprecated alias. Build, security review, and quality review use git-private worker runs under `.git/edc/runs/<run-id>/` and promote canonical context/reports only after staged outputs validate.

At the start of each source-research coordinator run, EDC probes an already-installed Octocode CLI once with a short timeout and reuses that immutable available/unavailable state for every source worker in the run. `review-all` passes its normalized state to child lens coordinators so parallel/serial phases cannot disagree. Caller-preseeded state is otherwise discarded. Octocode is optional and never installed by EDC; unavailable or failed semantic queries fall back immediately to native tools and cannot widen task scope or override manifest routing. Synthesis-only audit workers receive only the reporting contract, not source-research methodology or capability guidance.

## Actors and entrypoints
- Human operator invokes `edc build|update|review|review-all|security-review|delivery-review|quality-review|audit|mode|doctor` after install.
- Agent subprocesses are spawned through `edc_spawn` with `EDC_AGENT_CLI=claude|cursor|codex|pi`.
- Worker-pool tasks invoke `plugins/edc/scripts/edc-worker.sh`, which verifies task provenance then delegates to `edc_spawn`.
- Command wrappers and Pi jobs invoke trusted `runtime-bootstrap.mjs` from package source or the current user's managed `~/.edc`; it validates that source, rejects repo-local `.edc/` execution, and dispatches the colocated trusted orchestrator. Integrity failure writes structured results and fails closed.
- Slash-command wrappers in `plugins/edc/commands/` invoke the same scripts from Claude/Cursor surfaces.
- `install.sh` delegates managed runtime/private prompt copying to `runtime-manifest.mjs`; legacy private skill directories are removed, while public skill installers still copy only human-facing skills for host agents.

## Key files
- `plugins/edc/scripts/edc`: public CLI parser. It normalizes `--diff <base>...<target>`, maps combined/security/delivery/quality commands, enforces agent/mode choices, validates its colocated package/global source before sourcing config helpers, and dispatches every orchestrator through `runtime-bootstrap.mjs`. Repo-local and arbitrary fallback script lookup is intentionally absent.
- `plugins/edc/hooks/lib/runtime-bootstrap.mjs`: allowlisted orchestrator gateway. It accepts only package source or current `HOME/.edc`, validates the complete source/runtime inventory, spawns the selected Bash orchestrator in a detached process group, forwards TERM/INT/HUP, and escalates before an outer Pi supervisor. It does not install or repair repo-local state.
- `plugins/edc/scripts/edc-lib.sh`: shared path constants, timeout wrapper, idempotent safe config loading, model resolution, stream filters, cost/transcript logging, trusted-source preflight/fail-safe result writing, prompt rendering, review write-containment snapshots, worker-run/task helpers, and atomic promotion helpers. Its Bash fallback timeout atomically publishes the timer PID, arbitrates command-vs-watchdog completion, fails closed on timer/publication errors, reaps watchdog children, and restores caller TERM/INT traps. It probes Octocode once per coordinator and emits the cached capability guidance for source-research prompts; review-all children may inherit only the parent's normalized state. Managed prompts resolve only from the validated package/global runtime. `EDC_PARALLEL` must be `0`/unset or `1`; worker manifests use concurrency 1 unless parallel is explicitly enabled, then `EDC_MAX_CONCURRENCY` is validated as integer 1-64 (default 4).
- `plugins/edc/scripts/edc-agent-backends.sh`: backend-specific `edc_spawn` command construction and capture lifecycle, extracted from `edc-lib.sh` behind its stable public function.
- `plugins/edc/scripts/edc-review-plan.sh`: security review file discovery, classification, task-manifest construction, and task prompt planning. `edc-review.sh` loads it only after runtime integrity succeeds.
- `plugins/edc/scripts/edc-worker.sh`: production worker runner for the Node pool. It reads a validated task JSON file, checks `EDC_RUN_ID`/`EDC_TASK_ID`/`EDC_TASK_PHASE` against coordinator environment, requires the configured backend, and calls `edc_spawn` with `--prompt-file`.
- `plugins/edc/hooks/lib/worker-pool.mjs`: bounded coordinator. It validates manifest schema, rejects unknown fields and paths outside `runDir`, enforces output containment including symlink escape checks, starts workers in detached process groups, enforces task timeouts, kills siblings/queued tasks for fail-fast failures, supports `continue` policy, and writes `stage-result.json` in manifest order. Its TERM-to-KILL grace comes from the shared managed `termination-policy.mjs`, allowing Pi's outer background-job grace to remain longer than the nested worker grace.
- `plugins/edc/hooks/lib/worker-manifest.mjs`: turns JSONL task rows into a versioned worker manifest with run id, run dir, max concurrency, and tasks.
- `plugins/edc/hooks/lib/build-dag.mjs`: expands the validated build plan into module-context and build-audit worker manifests, staged prompt files, staged audit reports, and module metadata used by later build phases.
- `plugins/edc/scripts/edc-build.sh`: classifies context state, performs full build as a coordinator-owned DAG, or spawns the update prompt for healthy-v2 incremental updates. Full build inventory reads `git ls-files -s`, applies ignore rules, runs discovery, module workers, cross-module synthesis, assembly, build-time audit workers, report synthesis, manifest finalization, staged validation, clean promotion, doctor, curator report/edit, and final doctor. Its full-build task planning is now through `json-cli.mjs build-plan` plus `build-dag.mjs`; the old standalone `edc-build-plan.sh` script is gone.
- `plugins/edc/scripts/edc-update.sh`: healthy-v2-only incremental update gate; accepts Pi backend and uses normal `bash` resolution for preflight and doctor. The update prompt itself remains a single clean mutation worker rather than a fanout pipeline.
- `plugins/edc/scripts/edc-review.sh`: security/adversarial review pipeline. Every executable mode, including task-only `--build`, runs runtime preflight before loading review dependencies. It recovers freshness unless explicitly bypassed, delegates deterministic task planning to `edc-review-plan.sh`, runs security workers through the pool with `continue` policy, accepts substantive staged module prose, writes explicit coverage-gap reports for failed workers with no substantive output, consolidates/verifies one canonical staged final report, then promotes the final root review artifact.
- `plugins/edc/scripts/edc-audit.sh`: quality-review orchestrator. It preflights runtime integrity before lazily loading freshness/recovery helpers, recovers context, selects all modules or diff/dirty mapped modules, runs per-module audit workers through the pool, preserves substantive staged prose or writes explicit coverage-gap reports after worker failures, then gives synthesis only staged reports plus the reporting contract. Missing synthesis outputs become explicit canonical coverage gaps before promotion to `edc-context/reports/`. It removes staged audit-task IPC unless `EDC_KEEP_AUDIT_TASKS=1`.
- `plugins/edc/scripts/edc-review-all.sh`: combined review orchestrator. It resolves one candidate, prepares context once, runs security, delivery, and quality serially by default (or concurrently when `EDC_PARALLEL=1`) with per-phase `EDC_RESULT_FILE`s and git-private promotion staging, rejects staged outputs that are symlinks, hardlinks, non-regular, or resolve outside the run, then aggregates child structured results.
- `plugins/edc/scripts/edc-review-candidate.sh`: shared dirty-policy validation and immutable synthetic candidate creation. It captures staged, unstaged, deleted, and selected non-ignored untracked content through alternate indexes, recursively creates synthetic commits for dirty initialized submodules, and does not move refs/HEAD or mutate any real index.
- `plugins/edc/scripts/edc-delivery-review.sh`: delivery/architecture review pipeline. It preflights runtime integrity before lazily loading freshness/recovery helpers, remains single-prompt/single-report, validates refs, supports `--full`, embeds the delivery skill bundle, preserves substantive delivery prose, writes an explicit coverage-gap report when output is missing, and records structured results.
- `plugins/edc/scripts/edc-manifest.sh` and `edc-doctor.sh`: deterministic manifest finalization and v2 layout/routing validation.

## Core flows
### Coordinator-owned full build DAG
1. Shell decides route using `edc-clean-slate.sh --check`; v1 is refused and partial layouts are wiped only by the orchestrator.
2. Build inventory reads tracked file metadata with ignore rules, then a discovery worker writes a structured module plan without reading source bodies.
3. `json-cli.mjs build-plan` validates module names/paths and emits module-context prompts. `build-dag.mjs` writes module and build-audit task manifests.
4. `worker-pool.mjs` runs module-context workers; each writes exactly one staged module doc under `.git/edc/runs/<run-id>/staged/edc-context/modules/`.
5. Cross-module and assembly workers consume staged module docs/metadata, not source bodies, to write staged index, partial manifest, build metadata, and agent entrypoint.
6. Build-time audit workers and synthesis produce staged issues/complexity reports.
7. `edc-manifest.sh` finalizes the staged manifest; staged outputs are validated; only then are `edc-context/` and the agent entrypoint promoted.

### Security and quality worker stages
1. Review/audit orchestrators recover fresh context first unless the caller requested direct/no-context security mode.
2. Task files and prompts are written under the git-private run dir; declared worker outputs are also staged there.
3. The pool enforces concurrency, timeout, fail-fast/continue behavior, output existence, and containment. Canonical context and reports are treated as forbidden during worker stages.
4. Failed normal security and quality workers become warnings: substantive staged prose is preserved, while missing/empty output becomes a deterministic unavailable-coverage report. Security promotion-check tasks retain their structured report/result contract; missing delivery and quality-synthesis output is likewise promoted only as an explicit coverage gap.
5. Final reports are promoted atomically only after staged synthesis/consolidation and validation succeed.

### Optional source-research capability
1. Each top-level update/build/security/audit/delivery coordinator checks once whether `octocode` exists and whether `octocode --version` succeeds within two seconds; review-all child lenses inherit its normalized state.
2. The prompt receives exactly one capability state. Available guidance recommends a small number of batched structure/search queries followed by native exact reads; unavailable guidance forbids installation and requires immediate native-tool fallback.
3. Capability guidance inherits the worker's assigned target and evidence permissions. Call-graph/search results are evidence only; classifier/manifest routing remains authoritative.
4. Discovery, cross-module assembly, and audit synthesis do not need source-research guidance; audit/build synthesis receives only the reporting contract.

### Coordinated background termination
1. Worker-pool tasks run in detached process groups and receive TERM followed by KILL after the shared worker grace; serial mode still uses the same worker manifest/provenance path with `maxConcurrency: 1`.
2. `runtime-bootstrap.mjs` supervises the orchestrator process group with a longer grace, allowing nested pools to escalate and reap first.
3. Pi's outer background supervisor waits another margin beyond bootstrap's deadline. Pi marks status `cancelled` and clears live UI only after the selected process/group is confirmed gone; failed termination preserves truthful `running` state and keeps the watcher active.
4. The Pi JSON supervisor also handles HUP and broken stdout (`EPIPE`) without leaking its child.

### Pi subprocess spawn
1. `edc_require_agent_cli` requires `pi` and `python3`; trusted wrappers enter via `runtime-bootstrap.mjs` before shell orchestrators reach this spawn boundary.
2. `edc_spawn` writes or reuses a prompt file, then invokes `pi --mode json --no-session --no-context-files --no-skills --no-prompt-templates --no-extensions -p @file` with `EDC_PI_SUBPROCESS=1`.
3. If `EDC_PI_EXTENSION_PATH` is set, it must be an absolute readable file and is passed as exactly one explicit `-e <path>` while all other extension discovery remains disabled.
4. Worker processes receive `EDC_RUN_ID`, `EDC_TASK_ID`, `EDC_TASK_PHASE`, and optional `EDC_TASK_MODULE`; spawn logs/transcripts default to the run dir for worker phases.
5. `pi-supervisor.mjs` ignores `agent_end` events with `willRetry: true`, then classifies the terminal event so provider retry preambles do not prematurely fail the worker.

## Invariants
- Orchestrators and worker scripts must remain Bash 3.2-compatible; nested script calls must not rely on `EDC_BASH`.
- Dirty differential scope is binary: a dirty tree fails by default; `--include-working-tree` reviews one complete synthetic candidate and `--committed-only` excludes all working-tree state. Result candidate/inclusion metadata comes from the resolved snapshot.
- Deterministic coordinators own build-vs-update, candidate resolution, context recovery, task graph shape, serial-vs-parallel execution, worker concurrency, timeout/cancellation, write containment, staged validation, promotion, review-all aggregation, and structured results.
- Models receive prompts and declared outputs only; they must not launch agents, invoke skills as processes, choose subprocess flags, or write canonical context/reports directly.
- `manifest.policy.defaultMode` is preserved across builds/updates and only `edc mode` should mutate it directly.
- Optional research capability is coordinator-detected per run: EDC must not install or require Octocode, unavailable semantics are unknown rather than negative evidence, and query results cannot override assigned scope or manifest authority.
- Nested cancellation deadlines are ordered: worker process-group escalation completes before runtime-bootstrap escalation, which completes before the outer Pi background supervisor escalates; status becomes terminal only after termination is verified.
- `edc_spawn` is the sole backend-specific subprocess boundary and its implementation is loaded only after trusted-source preflight. Pi workers default to no extension discovery; `EDC_PI_EXTENSION_PATH` permits exactly one explicit observer entrypoint.
- Runtime code executes only from validated installed-package source or the current user's managed `~/.edc`. Repo-local `.edc/` is never read, created, repaired, or executed, even if its bytes or symlink target resemble a valid package. Managed global artifacts must be regular files whose bytes match metadata before syntax checks, smoke execution, review planning, result dispatch, or model spawning.
- Worker output paths must remain absolute paths inside the coordinator run dir; symlink escapes and missing declared outputs are failures.
- Public workflow taxonomy must stay clear across CLI help/docs/prompts/tests: combined review, security-only review, delivery/architecture review, and code-quality review are different products.

## Trust boundaries
- CLI args, git refs, config values, prompt files, task manifests, worker outputs, Pi JSON streams, staged reports, LLM-authored manifests, and optional executables discovered on `PATH` are untrusted until their boundary-specific checks pass. The Octocode probe establishes availability only, not authority or correctness of search results.
- `EDC_PI_EXTENSION_PATH` is privileged observability configuration: accept only absolute readable files, pass as an argument array element, and keep `--no-extensions` enabled.
- Git-private `.git/edc/runs/` is operational IPC/log storage, not source context. Canonical artifacts are promoted from it only after validation.
- Package/global runtime source is executable trusted state. Package source is checked directly; `~/.edc` additionally requires current-HOME identity, metadata, modes, fingerprint, and per-artifact byte integrity. Legacy repo-local `.edc/` is untrusted decoy state and must remain untouched. Integrity-failure results use an inline trusted writer rather than a rejected helper.

## Coupling
- Consumes `canonical-skills` through `resolve_prompt` and embedded review/audit/delivery bundles; prompt wording now assumes coordinator-owned workers and no nested agent launches.
- Mirrors path constants/routing semantics with `plugin-surface` (`edc-lib.sh` vs `hooks/lib/paths.mjs`, shell route helpers vs JS route helpers) and depends on its canonical inventory for package/global worker JS helpers and private prompt bundles.
- Used by `agent-wrappers` for trusted runtime-bootstrap dispatch of Pi background jobs, timeout extension, scope/default-base argument passing, structured status fields, model propagation, optional Pi observer extension propagation, and ordered nested process-group termination through the shared policy owned by `plugin-surface`.
- Pinned by `hardening-tests`, especially worker-pool containment/concurrency, build DAG routing, review/audit write containment, phase results, Bash alignment, package install/copy, and Pi backend tests.
- Invoked by `benchmarking` when benchmark harnesses use production security review or subprocess/model propagation.

## Fragility points
- `edc-lib.sh`, `edc-build.sh`, `edc-review.sh`, and `edc-audit.sh` coordinate multi-stage worker runs; small changes can affect all backends and all canonical artifact promotion. The Bash fallback in `run_with_timeout` is especially stateful: trap restoration, timer PID publication, outcome ownership, cleanup, and timeout status must move together.
- Build assembly has duplicated index-contract wording in prompt markdown and embedded shell prompt text; keep required section order synchronized with the v2 index contract.
- Worker pool correctness depends on process-group behavior, descriptor cleanup, timeout backstops, realpath/case-insensitive output ownership checks, and manifest validation; regression coverage belongs in hardening tests when changing it.
- Continue-on-failure semantics remain explicit: normal security workers preserve substantive prose or receive a deterministic coverage-gap report, while promotion checks still require their structured sidecar contract.
- Pi subprocess supervision depends on Pi JSON event names (`agent_end`, `willRetry`, `message_update`, `tool_execution_*`, `auto_retry_end`). Event-shape drift can make output silent or misclassified.
- Direct security-review context bypass modes intentionally trade context freshness for caller control; keep that explicit in help, docs, and structured failure hints.
